ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in the Cartesian coordinate system, the graph of the linear function \(y=kx+b\) intersects the x-axis and y-axis at points A and B, respectively, and it passes through the point \(D(-2, 6)\). It intersects the graph of the direct proportion function \(y=3x\) at point C, where the \(x\)-coordinate of point C is 1. What is the equation of the linear function \(y=kx+b\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Solve: When $x=1$, $y=3$. Let the line $y=kx+b$ pass through $(1, 3)$ and $(-2, 6)$\\
$\therefore$ $\begin{cases}6=-2k+b\\ 3=k+b\end{cases}$\\
Solving these, we get: $\begin{cases}k=-1\\ b=4\end{cases}$\\
$\therefore$ The equation of the function is $y=-x+4=\boxed{-x+4}$
